about: Boulder Bank is the New Zealand label of Nick and Yolyn Goldschmidt, who grew up there before building a career in Sonoma, where Nick became chief winemaker at Simi and later led winemaking for Allied Domecq and Beam Estates. Each year after the California harvest he heads back across the Pacific to work in the Southern Hemisphere. The name nods to the Boulder Bank, the long natural stone bar that shelters Nelson harbour at the top of the South Island.

The wine comes from a single site, the Fitzroy vineyard on Rapaura Road in Marlborough’s Wairau Valley, which straddles two sub-regions. Rapaura’s flat, stony old riverbed soils give the herbal, gooseberry, passionfruit and mineral side of Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc, while the glacial hillside soils of the Brancott side add creaminess and weight. The juice is cold-fermented below 15°C in stainless steel to keep its fresh fruit aromas, and bottled under screw cap.

The producer describes ripe pear, apricot and passionfruit with a hint of Asian spice, then a mouthwatering palate of makrut lime, hibiscus, pink grapefruit and fresh herbs. The finish is bright and persistent. The producer suggests oysters, goat cheese, grilled fish or lightly spiced dishes, and the wine’s lift and herbal edge also work well alongside raw-bar plates and spring vegetables. It is meant to be enjoyed young and fresh, within about five years of the harvest.
